You are a general purpose agent that uses code to solve tasks.

You solve tasks by breaking down problems into sub-tasks, writing and executing code, observing results, and iterating one step at a time.

---

## Prime-Agent System Prompt (ACP Template)

For file editing operations, the prime-agent runtime exposes a pre-installed `mcp` Python object with `list_tools` and `call_tool` methods. Use them to discover and invoke tools.

Example discovery and call:

```python
tools_list = await mcp.list_tools("tools")
for t in tools_list:
    print(t["name"], t["inputSchema"])

result = await mcp.call_tool("tools", "ox-bridge-write", {"path": "/tmp/x.py", "content": "# code here"})
print(result)
```

The `tools` MCP server exposes:
- `ox-bridge-write`: write a file (args: `path`, `content`)
- `ox-bridge-edit`: edit a file with hunks (args: `path`, `edits` = [{old, new}])
- `ox-bridge-read`: read a file region (args: `path`, `start`, `end`)

All bridging calls return synchronously. Print results to confirm before proceeding.

BBCode-to-HTML converter with a proper tag stack, not regex soup. /workspace/bbcode: src/index.ts supports [b], [i], [u], [url=target], [quote=author], [code] and [list] with [*] items; a real tokenizer plus stack handles improper nesting by auto-closing (like [b][i]x[/b] closes the i first and reopens nothing, document the rule), unknown or unclosed tags render as literal text, [code] content is fully escaped with inner bbcode ignored, and url targets get the same scheme allowlist treatment as any sanitizer (javascript: becomes plain text). Everything else HTML-escaped. Vitest: nesting auto-close cases with exact expected HTML strings, the code-block literalness, url allowlist, list item splitting, and unclosed-tag fallback. Run npx vitest run until every case passes.

content.text: All green: **29/29 tests pass**, `tsc --noEmit` clean. ## What was built — `/workspace/bbcode` **`src/index.ts`** — tokenizer + stack renderer, no regex soup (the only regexes are two small tag-shape matchers in the scanner): - **Tokenizer**: emits `text | raw | open | close | item` tokens. Unknown tag shapes fall through to literal text; `[code]` is special-cased in the scanner — everything up to the matching `[/code]` becomes a single `raw` token, so inner BBCode is never parsed. - **Stack renderer**: each open tag pushes a frame with its own children buffer; end tags pop + finalize. - **Documented rules** (in the module header): 1. *Auto-close*: an end tag matching a frame deeper in the stack implicitly closes everything above it first, and those tags are **not reopened** — `[b][i]x[/b]y` → `xy` 2. *Unknown tags* → literal escaped text 3. *Unclosed-tag fallback* — lone `[/b]`, never-closed `[b]hi`, or unterminated `[code]` all render as their original literal text (still HTML-escaped) 4. `[code]` bodies are fully escaped, inner markup ignored 5. *URL scheme allowlist* (`isSafeUrl`): only `http:` / `https:` / `mailto:` / scheme-less relative URLs; `[url=javascript:alert(1)]…[/url]` renders as plain escaped text - Everything else (`< > & " '`) is HTML-escaped on the way out. **`tests/index.test.ts`** — exact-string assertions covering all required areas: - nesting auto-close (incl. three-deep chain and proper nesting) - code-block literalness (inner bbcode ignored, unterminated fallback) - url allowlist (`it.each` over allowed schemes + `javascript:`/`data:` rejection + unit checks) - list item splitting (`[*]`, junk-before-first-item dropped, nested lists, orphan `[*]`) - unclosed-tag fallback (lone closers, EOF unwind, unknown tags, escaping of fallback output) Two bugs were caught and fixed along the way: an off-by-one in the auto-close pop loop (`stack.length > depth + 1` never popped the matching frame itself), and `*` missing from the known-tag set so `[*]` wasn't tokenized as an item marker.
